reason: Verified in the code and in Chromium's own accessibility tree, not inferred. lately.html chart() emits .gridline b, .record-tag, .bar-val, twelve .xaxis spans and the .sr paragraph as siblings under .chart, and not one of them carries aria-hidden; the only aria-hidden in that subtree are the icon SVGs and .ghost-plot. Walking the chart's text leaves at 1440x960, state=full, returns exactly the sequence the seat names: '6', '12', 'Best week · 8', '12 so far', then all twelve dates, then the sr sentence. CDP Accessibility.getFullAXTree confirms the invisible ones are live: '4 MAY', '11 MAY', '25 MAY', '1 JUN', '15 JUN', '22 JUN' and '6 JUL' all come back ignored:false with no ignoredReasons, because .xaxis span.mute { opacity: 0 } (line 260) removes them from sight but not from the tree — the textbook opacity-versus-visibility mistake. So a screen-reader user does get the twelve weeks twice: once as the sentence the .sr line was written to give, and once as loose numerals plus seven dates that are not on the screen. Two corrections to the seat's write-up, neither of which changes the verdict. First, the count is seven, not eight: show = i % 3 === 0 || i === 11 leaves five ticks visible (27 Apr, 18 May, 8 Jun, 29 Jun, 13 Jul) and seven muted, which I counted in the DOM. Second, the consequence reverses the order — .sr is the last child of .chart, so the furniture is heard first and the sentence last, which makes the duplication worse, not better: the reader wades through the noise before reaching the line that explains it. Severity 'defect' is the right class and I am not raising it. Nothing here is untrue and nothing fails to work; the sentence is still correct and still reaches the reader. It is visibly — audibly — wrong and passable. Not covered by either gate: interaction-check.mjs asserts the chart HAS a spoken equivalent (words.chartSpoken) and that no .sr sits under aria-hidden, but never that the visual layer is kept out of the tree, and audit.mjs's visibility test at line 206 checks visibility and display only, so opacity:0 text is invisible to it too. This is exactly the seam the brief asks findings to be spent on.
sharpenedFix:
The seat's fix works but is more attributes than it needs and leaves one chart silent. Sharpen it three ways. (1) Instead of tagging .gridline, .record-tag and .bar-val separately, put aria-hidden="true" on the
wrapper in chart() — it already contains all three plus .baseline and .cols, holds no .sr, and one attribute stays correct as the plot gains children, whereas three named hooks rot. (2) Keep aria-hidden="true" on
as proposed. (3) Change .xaxis span.mute { opacity: 0 } to { visibility: hidden } as proposed — layout is identical, the flex box is preserved either way, and it is the right primitive for 'not there'; do it even though (2) already covers the tree, so no invisible element carries live text at all. Then the piece the seat missed: the first-run chart (lately.html ~line 779) is a second, separate literal — its own .plot with a .bar-val reading ' so far' and a one-tick .xaxis — and it has NO .sr line. Applying aria-hidden there, which any class-level pass will, would take that chart from partly spoken to entirely silent. Add a short sr equivalent beside it in the same commit:

This week so far: ${D.thisWeek} jobs finished, week commencing ${D.weeks[11].start}. Twelve weeks of history are not recorded yet.

. That keeps the protected drawn-but-empty plot and the partial-bucket treatment intact while making the state say in words what it draws.
breaks: Low blast radius, but re-measure four things. (1) interaction-check.mjs reaches into this subtree three times — the gridline scale check (~line 254, querySelectorAll('.gridline') plus Number(textContent)), the partial-bucket check (~line 335, document.querySelector('.bar-val').textContent.includes('so far')), and the chartSpoken check (~line 326). All three are DOM queries, which aria-hidden does not affect, so all three should stay green; run the gate and confirm rather than assume. (2) The 'no screen-reader line is buried under aria-hidden' assertion (line 166, spoken.hidden === 0) is the one that can actually flip. It is safe for the main chart because .sr is a sibling of .plot and .xaxis, not a descendant — but it WILL fire if the new first-run .sr from the sharpened fix is placed inside .plot or .xaxis instead of beside them, and it must be checked in the loading state too, where movementOne() is rendered inside <div class="sk-wrap" aria-hidden="true"> (line 805) and survives today only because line 957 strips .sk-wrap .sr; a new sr line must be caught by that same strip. (3) audit.mjs line 206 treats visibility:hidden as invisible but has no opacity rule, so the seven muted ticks currently enter its contrast, type-ramp and hit-target passes and will drop out after the change. That can only relax the audit, never tighten it, but the pass counts will move and someone should not read the smaller denominator as a regression. (4) Re-shoot light-first-run--1440x960.png only if the sr addition is placed in a way that reflows; it should not, since .sr is a 1px clipped absolute box. Nothing visual changes in any other frame — aria-hidden paints nothing, and visibility:hidden occupies the same box opacity:0 did.
